So you may have seen my name, you may not have. I post a lot. I try to post as much content as I can while still making sure the content is unique, is posted from it's source or re-hosted to an image hosting site. And most of all, I try to put it in the correct subverse, including my own subverse for random content /v/gobacks.

When I'm not posting, I'm looking everywhere on the net for content and adding it to a list that i keep for later posting. When I'm on my computer, which is the easiest place to post from, I pull out my list and start posting. In my own subverse where I am usually the only contributor, I try an post five links per day. Often times, these links are posted at or around the same time. Today, I came up to this error which I've never got before

You have reached your hourly submission quota for this subverse.

This was of course annoying, but sometimes I fail to look at the bigger picture as to why such a block might be necessary and important for the community. So I wanted your thoughts on this restriction. Especially as it preotains to those posting to their own subvserses.
What are you thoughts on limits placed on posting too much content?

I'm sure that this measure was put in place to prevent spam. If the poster in posting unique content than I think that he shouldn't be limited, but the system has no way of telling what is unique content and what is spam.

I post often and I hit that bastard all the time. Even as I write this I'm at my limit for /v/Android, /v/News, /v/Technology, /v/Alaska, and /v/Gaming. I'm not a spammer, and the things I post are relevant to each subverse and are well received. I just hit the limit a lot.

Now, that said, I think it's a good measure to have in place. It limits me often, but I think that's a good thing. It keeps the homepage from being too homogeneous, consisting of posts from one or two people's perspective. It also has the side effect of making me post to smaller subs if I want to keep contributing that day. I've taken a bigger interest in /v/Alaska with my posting time and I've started my own small subverse as well as an outlet for one of my interests. Basically it makes you split your focus if you're someone like me who has an intense interest in one or two topics.

Recommendations: The Runelords by David Farland; Magician by Raymond E. Feist

The Runelords starts the Earth King series by David Farland. The Runelords gain power by using a magical rune to steal it from their subjects. They can improve their eyesight or looks or strength or stamina etc... by taking it from someone else. Interesting premise, with inherent magic.

Magician is the start of the Riftwar Saga by Raymond E. Feist. While there isn't much with the Rifts to start, there is at least one Island that Romans used to inhabit. A Tolkein inspired world of Dwarves and Elves meets a coming of age story of two boys.

What makes me feel like he had no love for this series is that it feels like he rushed through parts of it. I felt like he didn't do much on the world building area, and that he would mention things in the book and quickly move on from them as though he wanted you to forget he even mentioned it.
